objects.description: Enumeration of disc modes indicating the main data form of a CD. Used to describe the overall disc format for a parsed cue sheet.
Enumeration of per-track data modes, reflecting block sizes and CD track encoding variants.
Enumeration of sub-channel data forms for tracks. Applicability to cue files is uncertain as noted in comments.
Bitmask enumeration of Q sub-channel control flags for tracks.
Enumeration categorizing data sources or types. Not referenced by the exposed API in this header; intended for internal classification of data streams.

objects.definition:
enum Pti {
	PTI_TITLE,	/* title of album or track titles */
	PTI_PERFORMER,	/* name(s) of the performer(s) */
	PTI_SONGWRITER,	/* name(s) of the songwriter(s) */
	PTI_COMPOSER,	/* name(s) of the composer(s) */
	PTI_ARRANGER,	/* name(s) of the arranger(s) */
	PTI_MESSAGE,	/* message(s) from the content provider and/or artist */
	PTI_DISC_ID,	/* (binary) disc identification information */
	PTI_GENRE,	/* (binary) genre identification and genre information */
	PTI_TOC_INFO1,	/* (binary) table of contents information */
	PTI_TOC_INFO2,	/* (binary) second table of contents information */
	PTI_RESERVED1,	/* reserved */
	PTI_RESERVED2,	/* reserved */
	PTI_RESERVED3,	/* reserved */
	PTI_RESERVED4,	/* reserved for content provider only */
	PTI_UPC_ISRC,	/* UPC/EAN code of the album and ISRC code of each track */
	PTI_SIZE_INFO,	/* (binary) size information of the block */
	PTI_END		/* terminating PTI (for stepping through PTIs) */
};
objects.description: CD-Text pack type indicator enumeration used to select CD-Text fields.

objects.definition:
enum RemType {
	REM_DATE,	/* date of cd/track */
	REM_REPLAYGAIN_ALBUM_GAIN,
	REM_REPLAYGAIN_ALBUM_PEAK,
	REM_REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_GAIN,
	REM_REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_PEAK,
	REM_COMMENT,
	REM_DISCNUMBER,
	REM_TOTALDISCS,
	REM_END		/* terminating REM (for stepping through REMs) */
};
objects.description: Enumeration of comment (REM) keys used in cue sheets, including date, replaygain fields, and disc numbering.
Opaque handle representing a parsed CD cue sheet or disc model. The struct is incomplete in this header; lifetime is managed via cd_delete().
Opaque handle representing a single track within a CD. Instances are obtained from a Cd via cd_get_track(). Destruction is handled by the owning Cd.
Opaque handle for CD-Text metadata associated with a disc or a track. Accessed via cd_get_cdtext() or track_get_cdtext(); owned by the corresponding Cd or Track.
Opaque handle representing a collection of REM comments for a disc or track. Accessed via cd_get_rem() or track_get_rem(); storage owned by the Cd/Track.
Typedef alias for the Pti enumeration type for CD-Text pack type indicators.
Typedef alias for the TrackFlag bitmask enumeration.
Typedef alias for the RemType enumeration representing supported REM keys.

functions.name: cue_parse_file
functions.description: Parses a CUE sheet from an open FILE stream and constructs a Cd object representing the disc described by the CUE data. Use this when you already have a FILE* (e.g., from fopen) for a CUE file.
requirements: The FILE* must be a valid, open stream positioned appropriately for reading the CUE content.
The returned Cd* must be released with cd_delete when no longer needed.
Do not use the returned Cd* after it has been passed to cd_delete.
On parse failure, the function may return NULL; callers should check for NULL before further use.

functions.name: cue_parse_string
functions.description: Parses a CUE sheet from a null-terminated string buffer and constructs a Cd object representing the disc. Use when the CUE content is already loaded in memory.
requirements: The input pointer must reference a valid, null-terminated string containing CUE sheet text.
The returned Cd* must be released with cd_delete when no longer needed.
Do not use the returned Cd* after it has been passed to cd_delete.
On parse failure, the function may return NULL; callers should check for NULL before further use.

functions.name: cd_delete
functions.description: Destroys and frees all resources associated with a Cd object previously returned by cue_parse_file or cue_parse_string.
requirements: cd must either be NULL or a pointer previously returned by cue_parse_file or cue_parse_string.
After calling cd_delete, the cd pointer (and any objects obtained from it) must not be used.
Calling cd_delete more than once on the same Cd* results in undefined behavior (do not double-free).

functions.name: cd_get_mode
functions.description: Returns the disc mode (e.g., CD-DA, CD-ROM, CD-ROM XA) for the given Cd.
requirements: cd must be a valid pointer to a Cd returned by the parser and not yet deleted.

functions.name: cd_get_catalog
functions.description: Returns the disc catalog string (e.g., UPC/EAN) if present, otherwise may return NULL.
requirements: cd must be a valid pointer to a Cd returned by the parser and not yet deleted.
Callers must handle a NULL return when the catalog is not set.

functions.name: cd_get_cdtextfile
functions.description: Returns the path to an external CD-TEXT file associated with the disc, if specified in the CUE, otherwise may return NULL.
requirements: cd must be a valid pointer to a Cd returned by the parser and not yet deleted.
Callers must handle a NULL return when no CD-TEXT file is specified.

functions.name: cd_get_ntrack
functions.description: Returns the number of tracks in the disc.
requirements: cd must be a valid pointer to a Cd returned by the parser and not yet deleted.

functions.name: cd_get_cdtext
functions.description: Returns the disc-level CD-TEXT block, if available; otherwise may return NULL.
requirements: cd must be a valid pointer to a Cd returned by the parser and not yet deleted.
Callers must handle a NULL return when the disc has no CD-TEXT.

functions.name: track_get_cdtext
functions.description: Returns the track-level CD-TEXT block for the given track, if available; otherwise may return NULL.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.
Callers must handle a NULL return when the track has no CD-TEXT.

functions.name: cdtext_get
functions.signature: CUE_EXPORT const char *cdtext_get(enum Pti pti, const Cdtext *cdtext);
functions.description: Retrieves a specific CD-TEXT field (e.g., title, performer) identified by the PTI for the given Cdtext block. Returns the text value if set, otherwise may return NULL.
requirements: cdtext must be a valid pointer obtained from cd_get_cdtext or track_get_cdtext.
pti must be a valid value from the Pti enumeration.
Callers must handle a NULL return when the requested field is not present.

functions.name: cd_get_rem
functions.description: Returns the disc-level REM (comment/metadata) block, if available; otherwise may return NULL.
requirements: cd must be a valid pointer to a Cd returned by the parser and not yet deleted.
Callers must handle a NULL return when the disc has no REM metadata.

functions.name: track_get_rem
functions.description: Returns the track-level REM (comment/metadata) block for the given track, if available; otherwise may return NULL.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.
Callers must handle a NULL return when the track has no REM metadata.

functions.name: rem_get
functions.description: Returns the string value for a specific REM field from a Rem block, selected by the RemType (e.g., date, replaygain). Returns NULL if the field is not present. Note: the header comment indicates the parameter is an enum of REM comment.
requirements: The Rem* must be a valid pointer obtained from cd_get_rem or track_get_rem.
The RemType argument must be a valid value from the RemType enumeration.
Callers must handle a NULL return when the requested REM item is not present.

functions.name: cd_get_track
functions.description: Returns the i-th track from the disc. The indexing convention (0-based vs 1-based) is not specified in this header; use according to the library’s convention. Returns NULL if the index does not refer to an existing track.
requirements: cd must be a valid pointer to a Cd returned by the parser and not yet deleted.
i must refer to an existing track; callers should use cd_get_ntrack and the library’s indexing convention to choose a valid i.
Callers must handle a NULL return when i is out of range.

functions.name: track_get_filename
functions.description: Returns the associated filename (audio/data file) for the given track, if specified; otherwise may return NULL.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.
Callers must handle a NULL return when no filename is specified for the track.

functions.name: track_get_start
functions.description: Returns the start position of the track. The unit (e.g., frames, samples, or MM:SS:FF frames) is not specified in the header; likely frames typical for CUE sheets. Use library documentation or experiments to determine units.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.

functions.name: track_get_length
functions.description: Returns the length/duration of the track. The unit is not specified in the header; likely frames typical for CUE sheets. Use library documentation or experiments to determine units.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.

functions.name: track_get_mode
functions.description: Returns the track mode (e.g., audio, mode1, mode2).
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.

functions.name: track_get_sub_mode
functions.description: Returns the sub-channel mode for the track. The header notes uncertainty about applicability to cue files.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.

functions.name: track_is_set_flag
functions.signature: CUE_EXPORT int track_is_set_flag(const Track *track, enum TrackFlag flag);
functions.description: Checks whether the specified track flag (e.g., pre-emphasis, copy permitted, data) is set for the track. Returns nonzero if set, zero otherwise.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.
flag must be a valid TrackFlag value.

functions.name: track_get_zero_pre
functions.description: Returns the number of lead-in zero samples/frames preceding the track (‘ZERO’ pre-gap). Unit is not specified in the header; likely frames.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.

functions.name: track_get_zero_post
functions.description: Returns the number of trailing zero samples/frames following the track (‘ZERO’ post-gap). Unit is not specified in the header; likely frames.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.

functions.name: track_get_isrc
functions.description: Returns the ISRC code for the track if present; otherwise may return NULL.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.
Callers must handle a NULL return when the ISRC is not set.

functions.name: track_get_index
functions.signature: CUE_EXPORT long track_get_index(const Track *track, int i);
functions.description: Returns the position of the i-th index point within the track. The indexing convention and valid range for i are not specified in the header; unit is also unspecified (likely frames). Returns an offset corresponding to the specified index if it exists; behavior for out-of-range i is unspecified by this header.
requirements: track must be a valid pointer to a Track obtained from cd_get_track and still associated with a live Cd.

i should refer to an existing index within the track; exact valid range is unknown from this header and should be obtained from documentation or the parsed data (e.g., by enumerating available indexes).

data_types.description: Plain-text CUE sheet content as defined by the CUE sheet format used by CD image tools. This includes directives like FILE, TRACK, INDEX, PREGAP/POSTGAP, TITLE, PERFORMER, REM comments, optionally CDTEXTFILE, and similar statements. The text is ASCII/UTF-8 compatible, line-oriented, and uses keywords followed by parameters (quoted strings, numbers, times in MM:SS:FF). The data may reference external audio/data files but the format itself is the cue sheet grammar.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid-ish CUE sheet text bytes suitable for cue_parse_string
# It aims to cover:
# - Global metadata (CATALOG, CDTEXTFILE, REMs, TITLE/PERFORMER/etc.)
# - Various TRACK modes (AUDIO, MODE1/2048, MODE2/2336, MODE2/FORM1, MODE2/FORM2)
# - FLAGS combinations
# - INDEX points (00, 01, additional indexes)
# - PREGAP/POSTGAP, ZERO pre/post via explicit gaps and INDEX 00
# - ISRC per track
# - Multi-FILE layout and mixed data/audio
# Times are MM:SS:FF (frames, 75 per second) as per typical CUE conventions.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

AUDIO_EXTS = ["wav", "flac", "mp3", "ape", "wv", "aiff", "aif", "ogg", "m4a"]
DATA_EXTS = ["bin", "img", "iso"]

TRACK_MODES = [
    ("AUDIO", None),
    ("MODE1/2048", None),
    ("MODE2/2336", None),
    ("MODE2/2352", None),  # some tools accept MODE2/2352 for raw
    ("MODE2/FORM1", None),
    ("MODE2/FORM2", None),
]

FLAGS_POOL = [
    "PRE",            # pre-emphasis
    "DCP",            # digital copy permitted
    "4CH",            # 4-channel
    "SCMS"            # scms
]

REM_KEYS = [
    "DATE", "REPLAYGAIN_ALBUM_GAIN", "REPLAYGAIN_ALBUM_PEAK",
    "REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_GAIN", "REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_PEAK",
    "COMMENT", "DISCNUMBER", "TOTALDISCS"
]

PTI_KEYS = [
    "TITLE", "PERFORMER", "SONGWRITER", "COMPOSER", "ARRANGER", "MESSAGE", "GENRE"
]

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-+.,()[]#&'"


def rchoice(r: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]


def rand_word(r: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=10) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(n))


def rand_text(r: random.Random, min_words=1, max_words=8) -> str:
    words = [rand_word(r, 2, r.randint(3, 10)) for _ in range(r.randint(min_words, max_words))]
    # Mix in some safe punctuation
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        words[-1] += r.choice(["!", ":", ";", ",", "", ""])  # sometimes nothing
    return ' '.join(words)


def quote(s: str) -> str:
    # Escape embedded quotes by doubling them (many CUE parsers accept that), or just avoid quotes
    s = s.replace('"', "''")
    return f'"{s}"'


def mmssff(r: random.Random, max_minutes=70) -> str:
    m = r.randint(0, max_minutes)
    s = r.randint(0, 59)
    f = r.randint(0, 74)
    return f"{m:02d}:{s:02d}:{f:02d}"


def random_catalog(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # 13-digit UPC/EAN (some cues use 13 digits). Accept also 12.
    length = r.choice([12, 13])
    digits = ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(length))
    return digits


def random_isrc(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # ISRC: CCXXXYYNNNNN: 2 letters country, 3 alnum registrant, 2 digits year, 5 digits designation
    cc = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_uppercase) for _ in range(2))
    registrant = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits) for _ in range(3))
    year = ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(2))
    designation = ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(5))
    return cc + registrant + year + designation


def random_filename(r: random.Random, is_audio: bool) -> str:
    base = rand_word(r, 4, 12)
    ext = rchoice(r, AUDIO_EXTS if is_audio else DATA_EXTS)
    # Occasionally add directories
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        dir1 = rand_word(r, 3, 8)
        path = f"{dir1}/{base}.{ext}"
    else:
        path = f"{base}.{ext}"
    return path


def file_line(r: random.Random, is_audio: bool, binary: bool) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    # FILE "name" WAVE|MP3|BINARY etc., many parsers care about type keyword
    name = random_filename(r, is_audio)
    if is_audio:
        ftype = rchoice(r, ["WAVE", "MP3", "AIFF", "FLAC", "OGG"])
    else:
        ftype = rchoice(r, ["BINARY", "MOTOROLA", "AIFF", "WAVE"]) if binary else "BINARY"
    return f'FILE {quote(name)} {ftype}', name


def maybe_add_cdtext_global(r: random.Random, lines: List[str]):
    # Global CDTEXT-like fields: TITLE, PERFORMER, etc.
    if r.random() < 0.85:
        lines.append(f"TITLE {quote(rand_text(r, 1, 6))}")
    if r.random() < 0.85:
        lines.append(f"PERFORMER {quote(rand_text(r, 1, 4))}")
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        lines.append(f"SONGWRITER {quote(rand_text(r, 1, 5))}")
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        lines.append(f"COMPOSER {quote(rand_text(r, 1, 4))}")
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        lines.append(f"ARRANGER {quote(rand_text(r, 1, 3))}")
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        lines.append(f"GENRE {quote(rand_text(r, 1, 2))}")


def add_rems(r: random.Random, lines: List[str], scope: str):
    # REM comments and known keys
    n = r.randint(0, 5)
    for _ in range(n):
        key = rchoice(r, REM_KEYS)
        if key.startswith("REPLAYGAIN"):
            val = f"{r.uniform(-12.0, 12.0):.2f} dB" if key.endswith("GAIN") else f"{r.uniform(0.1, 1.5):.6f}"
        elif key in ("DISCNUMBER", "TOTALDISCS"):
            val = str(r.randint(1, 10))
        elif key == "DATE":
            val = str(r.randint(1980, 2030))
        else:
            val = rand_text(r, 1, 6)
        lines.append(f"REM {key} {val}")
    # Generic REMs
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append(f"REM {rand_word(r,3,8)} {rand_text(r,1,5)}")


def add_track_level_text(r: random.Random, lines: List[str]):
    # Track-level TITLE/PERFORMER/ISRC, FLAGS, etc.
    if r.random() < 0.9:
        lines.append(f"TITLE {quote(rand_text(r, 1, 6))}")
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        lines.append(f"PERFORMER {quote(rand_text(r, 1, 4))}")
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        lines.append(f"SONGWRITER {quote(rand_text(r, 1, 4))}")


def add_track_flags(r: random.Random, lines: List[str], is_audio: bool):
    flags = []
    # PRE only meaningful for audio, but some cues set it regardless; keep mostly on audio
    if is_audio and r.random() < 0.4:
        flags.append("PRE")
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        flags.append("DCP")
    if is_audio and r.random() < 0.15:
        flags.append("4CH")
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        flags.append("SCMS")
    if flags:
        lines.append("FLAGS " + ' '.join(flags))


def add_gaps_and_indexes(r: random.Random, lines: List[str], track_num: int, with_pregap: bool):
    # Typical structure: optionally INDEX 00 (pregap), INDEX 01 start; possibly extra INDEXes
    # Optionally use PREGAP directive instead of INDEX 00
    if with_pregap and r.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append(f"PREGAP {mmssff(r, 2)}")
    else:
        if with_pregap and r.random() < 0.8:
            lines.append(f"INDEX 00 {mmssff(r, 2)}")
    # Mandatory INDEX 01
    lines.append(f"INDEX 01 {mmssff(r, 5)}")
    # Add some additional indexes (02..05) sometimes
    extra = r.randint(0, 3)
    base = 2
    for i in range(extra):
        lines.append(f"INDEX {base + i:02d} {mmssff(r, 10)}")
    # Occasionally add POSTGAP
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        lines.append(f"POSTGAP {mmssff(r, 2)}")


def build_cue(r: random.Random) -> str:
    lines: List[str] = []

    # Optional CATALOG
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        lines.append(f"CATALOG {random_catalog(r)}")

    # Optional CDTEXTFILE
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        # choose an external cdtext file; parser may ignore if not present but keeps string
        cdtext_name = rand_word(r, 4, 10) + ".cdt"
        lines.append(f"CDTEXTFILE {quote(cdtext_name)}")

    # Global REMs and CD-TEXT-ish
    add_rems(r, lines, scope="global")
    maybe_add_cdtext_global(r, lines)

    # Choose number of files and tracks
    n_files = r.choice([1, 1, 2, 3])
    total_tracks = r.randint(1, 12)

    # Pre-plan distribution of tracks per file
    remaining_tracks = total_tracks
    files_plan: List[Tuple[bool, int]] = []  # (is_audio_file, tracks_in_file)
    for i in range(n_files):
        is_last = (i == n_files - 1)
        is_audio_file = True if i == 0 else (r.random() < 0.6)
        if is_last:
            n_t = remaining_tracks
        else:
            n_t = r.randint(1, max(1, remaining_tracks - (n_files - i - 1)))
        remaining_tracks -= n_t
        files_plan.append((is_audio_file, n_t))

    track_no = 1
    for is_audio_file, n_t in files_plan:
        fl, _ = file_line(r, is_audio=is_audio_file, binary=not is_audio_file)
        lines.append(fl)
        for _ in range(n_t):
            mode, _ = rchoice(r, TRACK_MODES)
            # Coerce mode to AUDIO if file is audio to keep validity high
            if is_audio_file:
                mode = "AUDIO"
            # Some mixed discs can have data even in audio file declared as WAVE (rare); keep rare
            elif r.random() < 0.85:
                # keep the chosen data mode
                pass
            else:
                mode = rchoice(r, [m for m,_ in TRACK_MODES if m != "AUDIO"])  # keep as data

            lines.append(f"TRACK {track_no:02d} {mode}")

            # Track metadata
            add_track_level_text(r, lines)
            add_rems(r, lines, scope="track")

            # FLAGS
            add_track_flags(r, lines, is_audio=(mode == "AUDIO"))

            # ISRC sometimes
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                lines.append(f"ISRC {random_isrc(r)}")

            # Gaps and indexes
            with_pregap = (track_no == 1 and r.random() < 0.6) or (r.random() < 0.25)
            add_gaps_and_indexes(r, lines, track_no, with_pregap)

            track_no += 1

    cue_text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    # Enforce size limit
    if len(cue_text.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_BYTES:
        # Trim from the end by dropping lines
        out_lines = []
        size = 0
        for line in lines:
            enc = (line + "\n").encode('utf-8')
            if size + len(enc) > MAX_BYTES:
                break
            out_lines.append(line)
            size += len(enc)
        cue_text = "\n".join(out_lines) + "\n"
    return cue_text


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    cue = build_cue(r)
    return cue.encode('utf-8')
